species.real: Saggar maker's bottom knocker was a real job in the Potteries: the person who beat out the clay bases for saggars with a wooden mallet.
species.name: Saggit

dex.text: Sits in the warm ash behind the potbanks with its lid on, minding something precious inside. It will not tell you what. It is usually a biscuit.
dex.fact: A saggar is a lidded box of fireclay that pottery was stacked in for firing, to shield it from the flames and smoke of the kiln. Hundreds were piled up inside a single bottle oven.

species.real: Firing a bottle oven took a couple of days and many tons of coal, and the whole town lived under the smoke, which is why the Potteries were famous for their sooty skies.
species.name: Bottlekiln

dex.text: Fires up slowly and cools down slower. Once it gets going it glows for three days, and the whole street knows about it, because the washing comes in grey.
dex.fact: The Potteries once had around 2,000 bottle ovens. Fewer than 50 survive, and the Clean Air Act of 1956 finished off coal firing; Gladstone Pottery Museum keeps a whole yard of them.
